lee: Heads-up: a new user reported the Go quickstart deadlocking on paginated reads when they enable parallel workers + token refresh. It sits forever and then we see soft 429s.
mina: Hmm, Go SDK uses a semaphore around in-flight cursors. Could be we hold a slot while auth refresh blocks and never release.
carlos: Repro: short-lived token refresh kicks in during processing; refresh path calls retry which blocks on a channel while holding the slot -> leak.
lee: Ouch. Two contributing things: (1) sample quickstart shows naive parallel spawn pattern, (2) SDK retry/auth paths don't always run release on all exit paths.
mina: Proposed fixes: make Release() idempotent in Go, ensure any path that sleeps/backoffs decrements in-flight before sleeping, and add a guardedAcquire that ties slot lifetime to a context that is cancelled on auth failure.
carlos: Also add a small example in quickstart showing ctx + defer release and a helper AcquireWithTimeout. Example snippet:```go
slotCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second)
if err := client.Acquire(slotCtx); err != nil { return err }
defer client.Release()
// do work
```
lee: Telemetry: emit client.active_slots and client.slot_leaks histogram. Console should warn if active_slots > max for >10s.
mina: PR plan: quickstart patch (hotfix) + docs note, Go SDK minor patch for idempotent release + AcquireWithTimeout, add unit test simulating token refresh fail.
ci-bot: CI queued for branch `hotfix/guarded-acquire` — will report status.
carlos: I'll open PRs and tag here. This should reduce onboarding confusion for any users running naive parallel paginators.
